newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo auction rubber prices seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Colombo auction rubber prices seen easing.

text.p: Rubber prices at the Colombo auction were virtually unchanged on Thursday and brokers and exporters said they expect prices to fall with increased quantities coming on the market.
"The market could be slightly easier next week with increased quantities coming in," said a broker at John Keells.
Best latex one-x was 75 rupees ($1.32), up 20 cents from Tuesday, when the auction was last held. No.1 was 73.50 rupees, the same as Tuesday while RSS 1 was unquoted on both days.
"We expect the market to come off as soon as the rubber starts coming in now the weather is good," said an exporter.
Brokers Forbes and Walker said 178 tonnes of crepe and nine tonnes of sheet were on offer on Thursday.
Prolonged rain since last month reduced Sri Lanka's rubber output to extremely low levels, traders said. The average offer at the auction is 200-300 tonnes.
Rain brings production to a virtual standstill and affects the quality of whatever can be tapped, they said. ($1=56.99 rupees) --Colombo newsroom
